definitions.gloss: somen; thin wheat noodles (usually served cold)
definitions.explanation: Very thin Japanese wheat noodles, typically eaten cold in summer with a dipping sauce (めんつゆ). Often written in kana, sometimes as {素麺|そうめん}.

examples.japanese: ⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧そうめん⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べたく→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: I crave somen in the summer.

examples.japanese: そうめん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{冷水|れいすい}→冷水：22480_reisui⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{締|し}めた→締める：10057_shimeru⟧。
examples.english: I rinsed the somen in cold water to firm it up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{流|なが}し→流し：18855_nagashi⟧そうめん⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{竹|たけ}→竹：02220_take⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{樋|とい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{流|なが}れて→流れる：01969_nagareru⟧くる⟦{麺|めん}→麺：14644_men⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{箸|はし}→箸：01026_hashi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧つかんで⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{遊|あそ}び→遊び：01285_asobi⟧だ。
examples.english: Nagashi-somen is a summer pastime where you catch flowing noodles in a bamboo flume with your chopsticks.

notes:
Very thin (about 1.3 mm or less) wheat noodles stretched with vegetable oil during production. A summer staple, usually eaten cold with a soy-based dipping sauce. Some regional varieties (e.g., {三輪|みわ}そうめん, {揖保乃糸|いぼのいと}) are well-known.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- そうめん⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{茹|ゆ}でる→茹でる：02324_yuderu⟧: to boil somen
- ⟦{冷|ひ}やし→冷やす：02403_hiyasu⟧そうめん: chilled somen
- ⟦{流|なが}し→流し：18855_nagashi⟧そうめん: flowing-somen (summer dish)
- そうめんつゆ: somen dipping sauce

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {冷|ひ}や{麦|むぎ}: slightly thicker cold wheat noodles
- ⟦うどん→うどん：05182_udon⟧: much thicker wheat noodles, usually eaten hot
- ⟦{蕎麦|そば}→蕎麦：14329_soba⟧: buckwheat noodles, eaten hot or cold
